newsitem.title: UK: Ockham sets Highway motor insurance revamp.
newsitem.headline: Ockham sets Highway motor insurance revamp.

text.p: British insurance managing agent Ockham Holdings Plc said on Thursday it had agreed terms with new investors for a capital expansion of its motor insurance business at Lloyd's in parallel with the sale of its aviation and non-marine business to Bermuda-based ACE Ltd.
The two transactions are with separate parties but together "will substantially transform the business of the Group", the company said in a statement.
Ockham said that investors in the motor transaction would include US-based Questor Partners Fund LP, other US-based investment funds and investment bankers Botts & Company Ltd.
Under the plan, which has to be approved by shareholders, the investors, and Ockham itself, will increase the capital base of Ockham Personal Insurance Holdings (OPIH) by up to 30.5 milion stg.
Ockham did not say how much other investors intended to put in, but said it would contribute up to 9.2 million stg itself.
The funds will be used to enlarge the capacity of the motor insurance business at Lloyd's, which trades under the name "Highway".

The board said the moves were in line with its strategic assessment that "returns to shareholders will be enhanced by moving resources away from the pure Lloyd's managing agency function...and towards direct participation in retail insurance and other financial services".
